agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In fs/smb/client/cifsacl.c, parse_dacl() trusted compare_sids() to identify the special NFS mode SID even though compare_sids() matches only the minimum subauthority count, so a short SID with only two subauthorities could be misclassified and then trigger an out-of-bounds read of sid.sub_auth[2].
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `ppace[i]->sid.num_subauth >= 3` before the `compare_sids(..., &sid_unix_NFS_mode) == 0` check in `parse_dacl()`, and the CVE/commit explicitly states that `compare_sids()` "only compares min(a, b) subauthorities," allowing a malicious ACE with `num_subauth = 2` and `sub_auth[] = {88, 3}` to still match `sid_unix_NFS_mode` and cause `sid.sub_auth[2]` to be read past the end of the ACE.
